title: Exponents, Prime Factorization and Order of Operations
seo_title: Grade 6 Exponents, Prime Factorization and Order of Operations Worksheets (TEKS 6.7A, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.7A generate equivalent numerical expressions using order of operations, including whole number exponents and prime factorization
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.7A: exponents, prime factorization, order of operations with exponents and grouping symbols, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An exponent tells how many times to use the base as a factor: 25 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
  • Prime factorization writes a number as a product of primes, often with exponents: 72 = 23 × 32.
  • Order of operations: grouping symbols, exponents, multiply and divide (left to right), add and subtract (left to right).

Examples

Example

8 + 2³ × 5

2³ = 8

8 × 5 = 40

8 + 40

Answer: 48

Example

Prime factorization of 36

36 = 4 × 9 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

Answer: 2² × 3²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying the base by the exponent: 2⁵ = 102⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
Working strictly left to rightDo exponents, then × and ÷, then + and −.
Stopping at a composite factorKeep splitting until every factor is prime.

faq.a: Generate equivalent numerical expressions using order of operations, including whole number exponents and prime factorization.
Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1.

faq.q: Do I multiply before I divide?
faq.a: No. Multiply and divide from left to right in the order they appear.

faq.q: How do I write a prime factorization?
faq.a: Use a factor tree, then group equal primes with exponents.

items.e: 5 is used as a factor 3 times, so the base is 5 and the exponent is 3: 5<sup>3</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 2 × signs).
2 is used as a factor 6 times, so the base is 2 and the exponent is 6: 2<sup>6</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 5 × signs).
7 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 7 and the exponent is 4: 7<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).
3 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 3 and the exponent is 4: 3<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).
10 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 10 and the exponent is 4: 10<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).

items.q: Which expression means the same as 64?
items.e: The exponent 4 says to use the base 6 as a factor 4 times: 6 × 6 × 6 × 6. It does not mean 6 × 4.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 35?
items.e: The exponent 5 says to use the base 3 as a factor 5 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. It does not mean 3 × 5.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 27?
items.e: The exponent 7 says to use the base 2 as a factor 7 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. It does not mean 2 × 7.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 93?
items.e: The exponent 3 says to use the base 9 as a factor 3 times: 9 × 9 × 9. It does not mean 9 × 3.

items.q: In 83, which number is the base?
items.e: The base is the big number that is multiplied: 8. The small raised number 3 is the exponent. 8<sup>3</sup> = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 is the value.
2<sup>5</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. Not 10: that is 2 × 5, the base times the exponent.
3<sup>4</sup> = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Not 12: that is 3 × 4, the base times the exponent.
4<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. Not 12: that is 4 × 3, the base times the exponent.
5<sup>3</sup> = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Not 15: that is 5 × 3, the base times the exponent.
6<sup>2</sup> = 6 × 6 = 36. Not 12: that is 6 × 2, the base times the exponent.
7<sup>2</sup> = 7 × 7 = 49. Not 14: that is 7 × 2, the base times the exponent.
2<sup>7</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 128. Not 14: that is 2 × 7, the base times the exponent.
9<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 9 × 9 = 729. Not 27: that is 9 × 3, the base times the exponent.
10<sup>4</sup> = 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10,000: a 1 followed by 4 zeros. Not 40: that is 10 × 4.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 36?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. 6 × 6 is not finished, because 6 and 6 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 60?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. 6 × 10 is not finished, because 6 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 90?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 90 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. 9 × 10 is not finished, because 9 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 100?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 100 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5. 10 × 10 is not finished, because 10 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: Which number has the prime factorization 2 × 2 × 3 × 5?
items.e: Multiply all the primes, including the repeated ones: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60. Adding them gives 12, and using each prime only once gives 30.

items.q: Which number has the prime factorization 2 × 3 × 3 × 5?
items.e: Multiply all the primes, including the repeated ones: 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 90. Adding them gives 13, and using each prime only once gives 30.

items.q: Which number has the prime factorization 2 × 2 × 2 × 7?
items.e: Multiply all the primes, including the repeated ones: 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 = 56. Adding them gives 13, and using each prime only once gives 14.

items.q: Which number has the prime factorization 3 × 3 × 7?
items.e: Multiply all the primes, including the repeated ones: 3 × 3 × 7 = 63. Adding them gives 13, and using each prime only once gives 21.

items.q: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. What is the GCF of 24 and 36?
items.e: Circle the primes the two lists share: 2 × 2 × 3. Multiply them: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists. Using each shared prime only once gives 6.

items.q: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 and 75 = 3 × 5 × 5. What is the GCF of 45 and 75?
items.e: Circle the primes the two lists share: 3 × 5. Multiply them: 3 × 5 = 15. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists.

items.q: 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 and 98 = 2 × 7 × 7. What is the GCF of 56 and 98?
items.e: Circle the primes the two lists share: 2 × 7. Multiply them: 2 × 7 = 14. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists.

items.q: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 and 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7. What is the GCF of 60 and 84?
items.e: Circle the primes the two lists share: 2 × 2 × 3. Multiply them: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists. Using each shared prime only once gives 6.

items.q: 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. What is the LCM of 8 and 12?
items.e: Use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in either list: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24. 8 × 12 = 96 uses the shared primes twice.

items.q: 9 = 3 × 3 and 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. What is the LCM of 9 and 12?
items.e: Use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in either list: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36. 9 × 12 = 108 uses the shared primes twice.

items.q: 10 = 2 × 5 and 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. What is the LCM of 10 and 12?
items.e: Use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in either list: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60. 10 × 12 = 120 uses the shared primes twice.

Factors of 4: 1, 2, 4. Factors of 10: 1, 2, 5, 10. GCF = 2. Multiples of 10: 10, 20. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. So LCM = 20. The GCF is never bigger than the numbers, and the LCM is never smaller.
Factors of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6. Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. GCF = 3. Multiples of 9: 9, 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18. So LCM = 18. The GCF is never bigger than the numbers, and the LCM is never smaller.

Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. GCF = 4. Multiples of 12: 12, 24. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. So LCM = 24. The GCF is never bigger than the numbers, and the LCM is never smaller.

Factors of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6. Factors of 10: 1, 2, 5, 10. GCF = 2. Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. So LCM = 30. The GCF is never bigger than the numbers, and the LCM is never smaller.

Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. GCF = 3. Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36. Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36. So LCM = 36. The GCF is never bigger than the numbers, and the LCM is never smaller.
7 + 2<sup>3</sup> × 4 = 7 + 8 × 4 = 7 + 32 = 39. Not 2,916: that comes from working strictly left to right.
3 × 5<sup>2</sup> = 3 × 25 = 75. Not 225: that comes from working strictly left to right.
5<sup>2</sup> + 6<sup>2</sup> = 25 + 6<sup>2</sup> = 25 + 36 = 61. Not 22: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
5<sup>3</sup> − 6 × 2 = 125 − 6 × 2 = 125 − 12 = 113. Not 238: that comes from working strictly left to right.
(6 + 4)<sup>2</sup> ÷ 2 = 10<sup>2</sup> ÷ 2 = 100 ÷ 2 = 50. Not 14: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(12 − 2)<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>3</sup> = 1,000. Not 4: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
2 × (3 + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 7<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 49 = 98. Not 22: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
6<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4 + 5 = 36 ÷ 4 + 5 = 9 + 5 = 14. Not 8: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
6 + 4<sup>3</sup> − 7 = 6 + 64 − 7 = 70 − 7 = 63. Not 993: that comes from working strictly left to right.
3<sup>2</sup> × 2<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 8 = 72. Not 36: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
4 + (5 + 8)<sup>2</sup> = 4 + 13<sup>2</sup> = 4 + 169 = 173. Not 73: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
9<sup>2</sup> − 3<sup>2</sup> = 81 − 3<sup>2</sup> = 81 − 9 = 72. Not 12: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
10<sup>3</sup> × 4 = 1,000 × 4 = 4,000. Not 120: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
4 × 5<sup>2</sup> − 2 = 4 × 25 − 2 = 100 − 2 = 98. Not 398: that comes from working strictly left to right.

items.q: Which part of 4 + 3 × 23 do you work out first?
items.e: 4 + 3 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 + 3 × 8 = 4 + 24 = 28. The exponent comes first, before × and +.

items.q: Which part of (5 − 2)2 × 4 do you work out first?
items.e: (5 − 2)<sup>2</sup> × 4 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 4 = 9 × 4 = 36. Grouping symbols come first, even before the exponent.

items.q: Which part of 20 − 2 × 32 do you work out first?
items.e: 20 − 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 20 − 2 × 9 = 20 − 18 = 2. The exponent comes first, before × and −.
2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 9 = 18. Marcus multiplied 2 × 3 first, but the exponent comes first.
10 − 2<sup>3</sup> = 10 − 8 = 2. Emma multiplied the base by the exponent, but 2<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
(2 + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> = 36. Noah squared each number, but the sum must be found first.
[19 + (6 − 1)<sup>2</sup>] ÷ 4 = [19 + 5<sup>2</sup>] ÷ 4 = [19 + 25] ÷ 4 = 44 ÷ 4 = 11. Work from the inside out. Not 6: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
2 × [7<sup>2</sup> − (4 + 5)] = 2 × [7<sup>2</sup> − 9] = 2 × [49 − 9] = 2 × 40 = 80. Work from the inside out. Not 100: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
9<sup>2</sup> − [4 × (6 − 3)] = 9<sup>2</sup> − [4 × 3] = 9<sup>2</sup> − 12 = 81 − 12 = 69. Work from the inside out. Not 60: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[(3 + 5)<sup>2</sup> − 4] ÷ 2 = [8<sup>2</sup> − 4] ÷ 2 = [64 − 4] ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30. Work from the inside out. Not 12: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
{2 × [5<sup>2</sup> − 6]} + 20 = {2 × [25 − 6]} + 20 = {2 × 19} + 20 = 38 + 20 = 58. Work from the inside out. Not 64: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
20 + [12<sup>2</sup> ÷ (6 − 3)] = 20 + [12<sup>2</sup> ÷ 3] = 20 + [144 ÷ 3] = 20 + 48 = 68. Work from the inside out. Not 41: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
[2<sup>2</sup> + 5<sup>2</sup>] × 4 = [4 + 5<sup>2</sup>] × 4 = [4 + 25] × 4 = 29 × 4 = 116. Work from the inside out. Not 56: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
(2 + 6)<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup> = 8<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 5<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 25 = 39. Work from the inside out. Not 13: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(23)2 × 9 = 49 × 9 = 4. Not 12: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.

items.q: Find the value of (12)3 + 38.
items.e: (12)3 + 38 = 18 + 38 = 12. Not 1 78: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
12 × (12)2 = 12 × 14 = 3. Not 36: that comes from working strictly left to right.
0.5<sup>2</sup> + 0.3 = 0.25 + 0.3 = 0.55. Not 1.3: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
4 × 0.2<sup>2</sup> = 4 × 0.04 = 0.16. Not 0.64: that comes from working strictly left to right.
10<sup>3</sup> × 0.45 = 1,000 × 0.45 = 450. Not 13.5: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
1.2<sup>2</sup> − 0.44 = 1.44 − 0.44 = 1. Not 1.96: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
(0.3 + 0.1)<sup>2</sup> × 5 = 0.4<sup>2</sup> × 5 = 0.16 × 5 = 0.8. Not 0.35: that comes from skipping the parentheses.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 36?
items.e: (2 + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> = 36. Without the parentheses, 2 + 4<sup>2</sup> = 18.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 54?
items.e: 2 × (1 + 2)<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 3<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 27 = 54. Without the parentheses, 2 × 1 + 2<sup>3</sup> = 10.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
2 × 3 + 12 = 32
items.e: 2 × (3 + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 4<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 16 = 32. Without parentheses, 2 × 3 + 1<sup>2</sup> = 7.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
1 + 3 × 23 = 32
items.e: (1 + 3) × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 8 = 32. Without parentheses, 1 + 3 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 25.

items.q: An amoeba splits into 2 amoebas every hour, and each new amoeba does the same. You start with 1 amoeba. How many amoebas are there after 6 hours?
items.e: Each hour the number doubles: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2<sup>6</sup> = 64. Not 12: that is 2 × 6. Not 32: that is only 5 hours.

items.q: A lab dish has 5 bacteria. The number of bacteria doubles every day. How many bacteria are there after 4 days?
items.e: 5 × 2<sup>4</sup> = 5 × 16 = 80. Find the power first. Not 10,000: that is (5 × 2)<sup>4</sup>. Not 160: that is 5 days.

items.q: Diego puts 1 penny in a jar on day 1, 2 pennies on day 2, 4 pennies on day 3, and keeps doubling. How many pennies does he put in on day 10?
items.e: From day 1 to day 10 the amount doubles 9 times, so day 10 is 2<sup>9</sup> = 512 pennies. Not 1,024: that is one doubling too many.

items.q: Jayden folds a sheet of paper in half 5 times. Each fold doubles the number of layers. How many layers are there now?
items.e: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2<sup>5</sup> = 32 layers. Not 10: that is 2 × 5. Not 25: that is 5<sup>2</sup>.

items.q: Valeria sends a message to 3 friends. In the next round, each of them sends it to 3 new friends, and so on. How many people get the message in round 4?
items.e: Round 1: 3. Round 2: 3<sup>2</sup> = 9. Round 3: 3<sup>3</sup> = 27. Round 4: 3<sup>4</sup> = 81. Not 12: that is 3 × 4.

items.q: A school has 5 buildings. Each building has 5 floors, each floor has 5 classrooms, and each classroom has 5 windows. How many windows are there?
items.e: 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5<sup>4</sup> = 625 windows. Not 125: that is 5<sup>3</sup>, the number of classrooms.

items.q: A square garden is 9 ft long on each side. What is its area?
items.e: Area of a square = side × side = 9<sup>2</sup> = 81 sq ft. Not 18 sq ft: that is 9 × 2. 36 is the perimeter in feet.

items.q: A box is a cube with edges 6 in long. What is its volume?
items.e: Volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge = 6<sup>3</sup> = 216 cu in. Not 18: that is 6 × 3. Not 36: that is 6<sup>2</sup>, only one face.

items.q: A square patio is 12 tiles long and 12 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
items.e: 12<sup>2</sup> = 12 × 12 = 144 tiles. Not 48: that is the perimeter, 4 × 12. 1,728 is 12<sup>3</sup>.

items.q: A puzzle cube is made of small cubes, 3 on each edge. How many small cubes make the puzzle?
items.e: 3<sup>3</sup> = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 small cubes. Not 19: that counts only the cubes you can see. Not 54: that counts the squares on all 6 faces.

items.q: Nevaeh puts a square rug with 6 ft sides on a floor that is 10 ft by 12 ft. How many square feet of the floor are not covered?
items.e: 10 × 12 − 6<sup>2</sup> = 10 × 12 − 36 = 120 − 36 = 84 sq ft. Not 108 sq ft: that uses 6 × 2 for the rug. Not 156 sq ft: subtract the rug, do not add it.

items.q: A square garden with 8 m sides has a square pond with 3 m sides in it. What is the area of the garden without the pond?
items.e: 8<sup>2</sup> − 3<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 3<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 9 = 55 sq m. Not 25 sq m: that is (8 − 3)<sup>2</sup>. Square each side first, then subtract.

items.q: Two boxes are cubes. One has 4 in edges and the other has 5 in edges. What is their total volume?
items.e: 4<sup>3</sup> + 5<sup>3</sup> = 64 + 5<sup>3</sup> = 64 + 125 = 189 cu in. Not 729 cu in: that is (4 + 5)<sup>3</sup>. Find each volume first, then add.

items.q: Emma has 2 square rugs. Each one has 3 ft sides. What is the total area of the rugs?
items.e: 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 9 = 18 sq ft. Not 36 sq ft: that is (2 × 3)<sup>2</sup>. Find the power first, then multiply.

items.q: A box holds 10<sup>3</sup> paper clips. How many paper clips are in 6 boxes?
items.e: 6 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 6 × 1,000 = 6,000 paper clips. Not 216,000: that is (6 × 10)<sup>3</sup>. Not 180: 10<sup>3</sup> is 1,000, not 30.

items.q: A square field has sides of 100 m. What is its area?
items.e: 100<sup>2</sup> = 100 × 100 = 10,000 sq m, which is 10<sup>4</sup>. Not 200: that is 100 × 2. Not 400: that is the perimeter.

items.q: A square photo has 5 in sides. It is enlarged so the sides are 10 in. How many times as large is the area now?
items.e: Old area: 5<sup>2</sup> = 25 sq in. New area: 10<sup>2</sup> = 100 sq in. 100 ÷ 25 = 4, so 4 times as large. The sides double, but the area is 2<sup>2</sup> = 4 times as large.

items.q: A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares. Which expression shows the number of squares?
items.e: 8 rows of 8 is 8 × 8 = 8<sup>2</sup> = 64 squares. 2<sup>8</sup> = 256 and 8 × 2 = 16 are different.

items.q: A square tile has sides of 0.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: 0.5<sup>2</sup> = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 sq m. Not 1 sq m: that is 0.5 × 2. Not 2.5: count the decimal places (2 in all).

items.q: A small box is a cube with edges 12 ft long. What is its volume?
items.e: (12)3 = 12 × 12 × 12 = 18 cu ft. Not 32: that is 12 × 3. Not 14: that is only (12)2.
